segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Hi Daniel, can you hear me? My headset's been acting up all week.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Hey Renata, yep, I can hear you fine. Thanks for jumping on again so quickly.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Of course. Sorry I'm a couple minutes late, I was stuck in the parking garage behind a delivery truck, which, working at a freight company, I guess I deserve.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Ha, occupational hazard. Did you ever get the bathroom renovation finished? Last time you said the tiles were three weeks late.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Don't get me started. Still waiting on the tiles. Anyway, Tomasz said he'll join around the halfway point, he's coming out of a sprint review.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Perfect, that works. So let me just recap the proposal we sent over last Tuesday so we're all looking at the same thing.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: The Lumenstack Pro plan lists at $38 per seat per month, and that includes 2 terabytes of monitored data ingest a month across all your pipelines.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Anything over that is billed at $0.40 per gigabyte, but based on what your team told us, you're sitting around 1.3 terabytes today, so you've got headroom.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: And the proposal was built on 45 seats on a 12 month term.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Right. Okay, so I'll be straightforward with you. We have a quote from Cartograph, and they came in at $29 per seat per month for basically the same seat count.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: So there's a pretty big gap there, and I- I need to be able to explain to our CFO why we'd pay the difference.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: That's fair, and I appreciate you sharing the number. Does the Cartograph quote include ingest, or is that metered separately?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Um, I believe it's metered separately. I'd have to double check, but I think it was 500 gigabytes included and then usage on top.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Okay, so that's a meaningful difference at your volume. At 1.3 terabytes you'd be paying overage on Cartograph from day one.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: That said, I do have some flexibility on price, but it's tied to term length. On a 12 month term I can do 12% off list.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: 12% gets us to what, about 33 and change?

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: $33.44 per seat. If you went to 24 months, I can take it to 18% off, which brings it to $31.16 per seat per month, locked for the full term.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Hm. 24 months is a bigger commitment. Let me think about that while we sort out the seat count, because I actually need to fix something in the proposal.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: The 45 seats is wrong. That was a typo on our side when I sent the headcount over. It's 54, five four. We flipped the digits.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Oh, good catch. So 54 seats, not 45. That changes the totals, I'll rework it.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Yeah, it's the 38 data engineers plus the 16 analytics folks who are on call for the dashboards.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Got it, 54. Oh, and it looks like Tomasz just joined.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Hey, sorry, sprint review ran over. Tomasz here, director of engineering. Hi Daniel.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Hey Tomasz, good to meet you properly. We were just at the part where Renata corrected the seat count to 54, and I'd put two pricing options on the table.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: 12% off on a 12 month term, or 18% off, so $31.16 per seat, if you commit to 24 months.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Honestly, from the engineering side, 24 months is fine. We're not going to rip out observability after a year. The migration off our homegrown alerting alone is going to take a quarter.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: One product question while I'm here. The Pro plan covers the Snowflake and dbt connectors, right? Those are the two we actually care about.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Yes, both are included in Pro, along with the Airflow integration. The only connector that costs extra is the mainframe one, and I don't think you need that.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: No, thankfully we retired the mainframe two years ago.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. If Tomasz is comfortable, then let's go with the 24 month term at the 18%.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Great. So 54 seats at $31.16 for 24 months. That's roughly $20,190 per year.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Now, on payment. Our standard is quarterly in arrears, we really don't love paying a full year upfront.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: I understand. The 18% on a 24 month deal is really built around annual upfront billing. Quarterly would pull that discount back down to around 15%.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Hmm. What about quarterly, but in advance, not arrears?

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: I can't do quarterly at the 18%, I'm sorry, that's a hard line from our finance team.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay. Then annual upfront, but I want net 45 payment terms on the invoice, not net 30.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Net 45 I can do. So annual upfront, invoiced once each year, net 45.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Fine, let's settle on that.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Can I jump in on timing? We'd originally talked about starting October 1st, but that's the week of our data center cutover, and nobody's going to touch onboarding that week.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Would the middle of the month work better?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: October 15th. Let's make that the start date instead.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Works for me, the 15th.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: The other thing, and this is a blocker for us, our security team needs your completed security questionnaire before legal will sign anything. We use the SIG Lite.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And we'll need your DPA, plus the latest SOC 2 Type II report.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: No problem, we have a completed SIG Lite on file. I'll send the questionnaire, the DPA, and the SOC 2 report over by Friday.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Speaking of onboarding, one thing I'd love to see is the onboarding package thrown in for free. Your proposal lists it at $6,000.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: That would help us a lot, honestly, with the migration.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: I hear you. I can't commit to that on this call. I'd need to take it to my manager, Jon, and see what's possible given we're already at 18%.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay, but please do ask. It'd make this a much easier sell internally.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: I will. So, next steps. I'll send a revised order form with 54 seats, 24 months, 18% off, annual upfront, net 45, and an October 15th start, by Thursday end of day.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And once I have that, I'll route it to our legal team. Joan Park in legal handles vendor contracts, she usually turns things around in five business days.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: I'll get our security team to review the SIG Lite as soon as it lands, so it doesn't hold up Joan.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Perfect. Oh, one thing I should've asked. Tomasz, you mentioned the analytics team might grow next year?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Yeah, we might add another 10 seats or so in the spring if the new BI team gets approved.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Which raises something. If we add seats mid-term, do those get the same 18% rate, or are they at list?

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: That's a good question. I honestly don't know how our deal desk handles mid-term adds on a multi-year contract. Let me find out.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Okay, because that'll matter for the business case.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: I'll put it to our deal desk today and mention it in the email with the order form, but I can't promise an answer by Thursday.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Anything else before we drop?

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Nope, that's it from me. I've got to run, we have a cutover dry run at three.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Same. Talk soon, Daniel.

segments.speaker: user
segments.text: Thanks both, talk soon.
